title: How much is a home battery worth on a time-of-use tariff if it is dispatched optimally?
summary: Replaces the fixed dispatch rule of energy-tou with a linear program (HiGHS) over 10 seeded synthetic weather years and the same assumed three-band tariff. A 10 kWh battery behind 6 kW of PV breaks even at $867/kWh installed under optimal dispatch with perfect foresight, against $674 for the best fixed rule and $444 on a flat tariff; with life limited to 4,000 full cycles it is $742, 10% above the rule and still under the assumed $800. A rolling 36 h plan with a perfect forecast matches the whole-year optimum to $1. The optimiser adds $33 to $108/kWh across 2.5–20 kWh, and a wear-aware optimiser adds $43–58 when cycle life binds. Stylised: perfect foresight, assumed tariff, synthetic weather, crude cycle-count degradation.
lede: how much is a home battery worth on a time-of-use tariff with optimal dispatch? An LP breaks even at $867/kWh for 10 kWh behind 6 kW PV, against $674 for the best fixed rule ($742 with a 4,000-cycle life); a rolling 36 h plan matches the year optimum (`energy-tou` with an optimiser).
